title: Boost — leverage
heading: Liquidation: the level, the buffer, which number to believe
text: Boost borrows in a public market — USDC against XAUt0 on Morpho, Arbitrum One. Its liquidation loan-to-value is 77% , written on chain and readable by anyone on the market page . Reach it and a liquidator repays part of your loan and takes gold for it: no phone call, no grace period, nothing to negotiate. As a price, at 3× with gold near US$4,376/oz that level sits around US$3,789/oz . Write your own number down before you open anything, and check the live one in the app. The Boost screen is more flattering than the market. Its "Gold can fall X%" safety buffer, its liquidation price and its health-factor dial are all calculated against a liquidation level above 77%. The buffer it prints is wider than you have, and the liquidation price it prints sits below the price that will actually close you. Plan against 77%, treat a Boost health factor near 1.1 as the line rather than 1.0, and read the buffer as the optimistic end of a range. We are reconciling this in the product. 2x 50% 3x 67% 4x+ 82% blocked at 82% Higher multipliers start much closer to the line. Boost is blocked above 82%. At 3×, gold must fall about 13% from today's price to reach the market's liquidation level; at 4× it takes under 3%. The forced exit. Gold drifts down 10%, your LTV goes 67% → 74%, a loan-health alert fires. Gold slips another 4%, the LTV crosses 77%, and a liquidator clears part of your debt with your gold at whatever price gold is at — realised whether you were watching or not. Any equity left is still yours, but if gold rallies next week you are no longer in the position to benefit. The liquidator is also paid an incentive out of the position, so liquidation costs more than the arithmetic above; the exact penalty here is UNKNOWN .

title: Boost — leverage
heading: What it costs to hold
text: You pay interest on the borrowed portion — (m − 1) × commit — for as long as the position is open, and that rate floats with supply and demand in the lending market. When we last checked it was near 3.5% and had already moved within the hour. Never plan on a fixed number; the live APR is shown in the app and on the site. On the 3× example, US$20,000 near 3.5% is roughly US$58 a month — about 7% a year against the US$10,000 you committed, which is the number that matters. Go sideways for a year at 3× and you are down roughly 7% with a narrower buffer, because the debt grew and the collateral did not. Leverage decays in a flat market. Whether Auri's 0.49% buy and sell fee applies inside Boost is UNKNOWN — the review screen shows no fee line. See Fees and limits .

title: Boost — leverage
heading: Before you start
text: Pro mode on. Boost does not exist in the app until you enable Pro mode in Profile : "leverage your gold for more exposure. For experienced users." No standard loan open. The two are mutually exclusive, and the consequence is easy to miss: while boosted, you cannot borrow cash . If you might need a draw, take the standard loan instead. Free gold to commit. Only unpledged gold qualifies; chips are offered at $500 / $1,000 / $2,500 / max free. Accept that the gold is unspendable. It is all collateral — no selling, gifting, sending or remitting until you close. A loss number, decided in advance. Before you touch the slider, not after.

title: Boost — leverage
heading: Open a position
text: Open Boost. With Pro mode on it appears in the navigation and in Actions. Pick the Boost tab; Standard loan beside it is the unlevered product. Enter your commit and set the multiplier. The commit is your equity and the most you can lose. As you drag the slider, watch the LTV and liquidation price move, not just the exposure figure. Read the scenario panel as a loss. It shows a ±10% gold move against the unlevered outcome. Look at the down case and ask whether you would hold through it. Check the review screen, then confirm. Multiplier, gold price, commit, exposure, cash borrowed, new LTV, liquidation price. Convert the gap between today's price and the liquidation price into a percentage yourself. On confirm, the debt starts accruing and the liquidation level is live.

title: Boost — leverage
heading: Manage and exit
text: The open-position panel shows commit, exposure, cash borrowed, entry price, current price, liquidation price and unrealised P&L. Watch the gap between current and liquidation price, not the profit line. You can close 25%, 50% or 75% — the panel shows the gold freed and loan repaid — or close entirely, which sells enough gold to clear the debt and returns the rest as free gold. Partial closing is the deleveraging lever: it lowers LTV and widens the buffer. The panel offers reducing, not reinforcing. There is no "add more gold" button, so in a falling market your only lever is to shrink the position — and shrinking realises the loss on the part you close. Whether adding collateral will be supported is UNKNOWN . Plan your exit assuming reducing is all you get.

title: Boost — leverage
heading: When not to use Boost
text: If losing the commit would hurt. Not annoy — hurt. Assume the whole thing can go. If you cannot check weekly at minimum. Gold trades continuously and there is no margin call to prompt you. If the multiplier is what makes the trade interesting. Boost only makes sense if you wanted the gold anyway. If the price just ran and you feel late. That is when leverage is most expensive and the buffer most likely to be tested. Alongside a recurring buy. Auto-Invest survives drawdowns by buying through them; leverage removes you from the market during one. For rewards. Borrowing earns Jewels. Jewels are a rounding error against a liquidation. Size it backwards from the loss Start from the loss you can absorb: commit = tolerable loss ÷ (multiplier × the fall you accept as plausible) . If you can absorb US$2,000 and treat a 15% fall as plausible, at 2× your commit is US$6,667 — not "whatever is free in my vault". The same tolerance at 4× allows only US$3,333, and buys a buffer under 3%. Higher multipliers don't let you commit more; they force you to commit less. The floor: equity is gone entirely on a fall of 1 / m — 50% at 2×, 33% at 3×, 20% at 5×. Liquidation always arrives first, which is what stops you owing more than you put in.

title: Boost — leverage
heading: What can go wrong
text: "Boost isn't in my navigation." Pro mode is off. Turn it on in Profile. "It says to repay my loan first." A standard loan is open. Repay it in full, or use that instead. "My commit is capped below my gold balance." The rest is pledged; only free gold counts. See locked versus free gold . "I was closed out without being asked." That is liquidation working as designed — in the lending market at 77% LTV, not at Auri's discretion, and it does not wait for you. "I closed part of it and my loss got bigger." Closing realises the loss on that portion. It reduces risk; it cannot undo a fall.

title: How your gold is held
heading: How your gold is held
text: Auri never takes possession of your gold. You own Tether Gold — one troy ounce of vaulted physical metal per token — at a blockchain address tied to your account, and any loan you take sits in a public lending market anyone can inspect without an Auri login. This page sets out that structure precisely, names the companies genuinely on the other side of your holdings, and lists what Auri has not yet published well enough for you to verify.

title: How your gold is held
heading: What you actually own
text: When you buy, your money does not become a line item in an Auri account. It is converted to USDC on regulated payment rails, swapped into Tether Gold, and credited to a self-custody vault address belonging to your account. The token carries six decimals, so your balance is denominated in troy ounces to six places — the smallest holding is 0.000001 oz. Each whole token represents one troy ounce of physical gold vaulted by Tether Gold's custodian. The consequence most gold apps blur: your claim on metal is a claim on Tether Gold's reserves, not on Auri. Auri is the interface, routing and pricing layer. It is not the vault, the issuer or the lender. title: How your gold is held
heading: XAUt and XAUt0 — why there are two tickers
text: Native Tether Gold (XAUt) exists only on Ethereum mainnet. Auri runs on Arbitrum, so the asset you hold is XAUt0 , the LayerZero OFT version of the same gold. The model is lock-and-mint against a single canonical reserve. Native XAUt is locked in an adapter contract on Ethereum at 0xb9c2321BB7D0Db468f570D10A424d1Cc8EFd696C , and an equal amount of XAUt0 is minted on the destination chain. Moving between chains is an atomic burn-and-mint: burning XAUt0 unlocks the original XAUt. Total XAUt0 is therefore bounded by the XAUt in that adapter, which is itself backed one-for-one by vaulted metal. XAUt0 is not a token with its own separate reserve, and not an unbacked bridge IOU. It is still a layer, and two things follow. First, the redeemable asset is Ethereum XAUt — reaching physical metal means unwinding to Ethereum, then following Tether Gold's own redemption process, whose minimum, fee and lead time are UNKNOWN in Auri's material. Second, XAUt0 tracks gold only while the adapter and the cross-chain messaging layer work as designed. A bridged representation can break while the underlying asset is fine. If that layer failed, XAUt0 on Arbitrum could stop tracking XAUt even with every physical bar untouched. Neither Auri nor Tether Gold can repair it. If you want gold with no cross-chain layer at all, XAUt0 is the wrong instrument for you. Physical gold one troy ounce per token, vaulted XAUt on Ethereum locked in an adapter XAUt0 on Arbitrum minted 1:1 against it Your vault only your keys move it Burning XAUt0 unlocks the original XAUt. Auri is not in the custody path. Auri appears nowhere on the path between your address and the vaulted bars — which also means Auri cannot repair that path if part of it breaks.

title: How your gold is held
heading: Your keys, your address, your account
text: Sign-in is passwordless via Privy — a passkey, or a six-digit code by email or phone, with Face ID or fingerprint unlock on mobile. In Profile , Self-custody vault address shows the address holding your gold, and Linked wallets lets you attach your own. Gifts, sends and cross-border transfers always require step-up authentication, as do sells and withdrawals to an external wallet: a passkey approval, or two six-digit codes, one emailed and one from your authenticator app. Auri cannot approve that step for you. Bank and Interac withdrawals can only go to an account in your own name — third-party payouts are not permitted. The one-time identity check applies to bank, Interac and debit-card methods only. Funding or withdrawing USDC from your own wallet requires no ID. Every transaction expands in Activity into its individual legs with transaction hashes and references, so you can audit each step rather than trust a summary line. The limit of the phrase "your keys". Auri has not published an exact key-custody description. Whether the signing key lives only on your device, whether it is split with an infrastructure provider, whether you can export it, and what account recovery requires are all UNKNOWN. Until that is documented, treat the vault address as yours to direct through Auri, not as a wallet you could walk away with.

title: How your gold is held
heading: The four moments when your value sits elsewhere
text: In the steady state Auri holds none of your money: gold and USDC are on-chain at your address. Four windows are different, and a trust page that omits them is misleading. A fiat leg is in flight. With Interac e-Transfer in Canada, a bank transfer in the US, or a debit card, the money is with a payment partner between leaving your bank and appearing as USDC — and in reverse on a withdrawal, quoted at one to two business days. That window is not self-custodial in any sense. Payment partner names: UNKNOWN. A loan is open. Collateral is posted into the Morpho market and your gold splits into locked and free. Locked gold cannot be sold, gifted, sent or remitted until you repay or unlock it. See borrow.html . A gift is unclaimed. Gifted gold sits in an escrow contract on Arbitrum until claimed. You can remind or cancel, and cancelling returns the gold to you. See gift-send.html . A Boost position is open. The same collateral, at a far higher loan-to-value. See boost.html . Legal ownership is the largest gap on this page. The on-chain design is intended to mean your gold is never an Auri liability and never reachable by Auri's creditors. The instruments that would prove it — the ownership structure (bailment, trust or bare custody), the insolvency treatment, and a statement that customer assets never appear on Auri's balance sheet — are UNKNOWN and unpublished. Judge that gap yourself rather than accepting the architecture as a substitute for it.

title: How your gold is held
heading: The proof surface, field by field
text: The reserves banner on Home , the Audited reserves tile and Live loan book all open a two-tab proof view. The Gold reserves tab shows live spot, a "100% backed" statement, a link out to gold.tether.to , and a metric grid: ounces in the vault, reserve value at spot, total tonnage and the attestation period — plus a personal table listing your holding, its physical backing, the custodian, your allocation and the last attestation date. The Live loan book tab shows the Morpho market metrics, the contract address, and a link to open the loan book directly. The number to sanity-check is the attestation date — if it is older than the stated cadence, treat the page as stale. Read the gold figures at the source. They mirror Tether Gold's public data: Tether's figures and Tether's attestation, not an Auri attestation of Auri's own holdings. The current build's reserve tiles are placeholder values and show two attestation dates that disagree with each other, so do not rely on them yet. The loan-book tab does read live. Headline numbers also need a timestamp with a named timezone, and Auri has committed to no publication cadence in writing — UNKNOWN.

title: How your gold is held
heading: What an attestation does not prove
text: It is usually not an audit. Reserve engagements of this kind are commonly structured as agreed-upon procedures, where the practitioner performs specified procedures and reports findings without providing an opinion or conclusion . That is materially weaker than a financial-statement audit, and calling it an audit is inaccurate. It is a snapshot. It describes one moment, and says nothing about the day after or what happened between two snapshots. Its scope is the gold behind the token, not the operator. It does not address Auri's solvency, other liabilities or equity. A clean reserves report and a failing company are perfectly compatible. A SOC 2 is not a reserves proof. It covers controls, not the existence of the assets. It does not prove your balance is included. A total is not evidence about you. That needs a per-user proof: an allocation view when logged in, and a login-free reconciliation you can check without one. The firm should be named and host its own report. The attesting firm, engagement type and standard applied are UNKNOWN as Auri-confirmed facts. Hosting the report on the firm's own domain removes the "you could have edited that PDF" objection entirely. None of this exists today: a public, login-free reconciliation of customer balances against the bar list; a downloadable bar-level file with serial numbers, fine weight, fineness and refiner; a CSV you can re-add in a spreadsheet to confirm client balances do not exceed the fine weight held; or a dated machine-readable feed of holdings and claims. Treat their absence as a limit on what you can verify right now.

title: How your gold is held
heading: The lending market is public — go look at it
text: Auri's loans are USDC borrowed against XAUt0 in one Morpho market on Arbitrum One, market id 0xed3f9a960d927791a354cc4549b1b44af9dd06c11566ea9d0bff66b8e4969610 . No account is needed: open it on Morpho . What you can verify there instead of taking Auri's word for it: The liquidation parameter. The on-chain LLTV is 77%. That is the level at which liquidation becomes possible — a ceiling to stay well clear of, not headroom to spend. Your exact liquidation level, liquidation price and health factor are shown live in the app; read borrow.html#liquidation before borrowing. The rate floats. It is not fixed. We observed roughly 3.48% and then roughly 3.70% on the same market within an hour. Any rate on a screen is a reading, not a promise. The oracle. Liquidation is decided by the market's price oracle at 0xA576e986ADD337Ff09a57d7778C477d27ee7bF8b — not by the gold price on Auri's site or in the app header. Those are display feeds; the oracle is the one with consequences. The size. This market is small. On a direct check, around US$2,051 of USDC was available to borrow against roughly US$15,027 of collateral, with a single supplying vault, Steakhouse High Yield USDC. Both figures move constantly and a market this size may not fill a large borrow. Check live before planning around it. Whether your specific position can be managed from a wallet you control, without Auri's app, is UNKNOWN. The market is public; the addressing of your individual position is undocumented. Ask before you borrow.

title: How your gold is held
heading: The stablecoin half of the story
text: Gold-token issuers routinely skip this. Auri's cash balance is USDC issued by Circle, and an Auri loan is a debt denominated in USDC — a second issuer sits inside your position whether you think about it or not. If USDC traded below a dollar, your cash buys less gold than its face value suggests; a USDC loan is an obligation in a unit that can itself move, in both directions. Read circle.com/transparency with the same scepticism this page asks for. Note too that the underlying assets are USD-referenced: the 45 residence countries and 28 display currencies in the app are presentation only, so if you live outside the US, currency movement affects you on top of the gold price. See reference.html .

title: How your gold is held
heading: If Auri stopped operating tomorrow
text: This is the question that matters, and it splits into three — only one of which has a clean answer today. Could you still reach your tokens? The assets are at an address, not in an Auri database, so they would still exist. Whether you could move them without Auri depends entirely on the key-custody model above, which is UNKNOWN. This is the single most important thing left to document. Could you still manage your loan? The market is public and its parameters live on-chain, so it keeps functioning, keeps accruing interest and keeps liquidating positions that cross the threshold regardless of Auri's status. Whether your position is addressed by a wallet you can sign for is again UNKNOWN — and this matters more than it sounds, because an open loan you cannot repay is a position that liquidates itself. Could you still get physical gold? That was never Auri's to give. Redemption is Tether Gold's process, on Tether's terms, starting from native XAUt on Ethereum. Minimum, fee and lead time: UNKNOWN here — read them from Tether directly. What does not depend on Auri: the bars, Tether Gold's attestation, the existence and parameters of the Morpho market, and the on-chain record of every transaction you have made. What does: the app, the pricing layer, the fiat rails, and — until the key model is published — your practical ability to act on your own holdings. The honest reading is that the asset layer is genuinely independent and the access layer is not yet proven to be.

title: Risks
heading: Gold price risk
text: What it is. Gold pays no dividend, no interest and produces no earnings. Only what the next buyer will pay moves its value, so it can fall and stay below your purchase price for a long time. What it feels like. You bought at a number you remember, the app shows a smaller one, and there is nothing to do but wait or sell at a loss. If you borrowed, the same fall pushes you toward liquidation . What limits it. Nothing limits the price — only your position size relative to your savings limits the damage, which is why Auri does not tell you what share of your savings to hold in gold. Two costs compound it: a round trip is about 1% (0.49% to buy, 0.49% to sell), and your order executes when your money lands, not when you tap — instant rails take minutes, a bank transfer one to two business days, and gold moves in that gap. See Reference . The projection calculator in Auto-Invest assumes a constant 8.5% a year and excludes fees and taxes. That is an assumption hard-coded so the tool can draw a line. It is not a forecast.

title: Risks
heading: Liquidation risk when you borrow
text: What it is. Borrowing pledges your gold rather than selling it: it is posted as collateral on a lending market and you receive stablecoins against it. If the collateral falls far enough relative to what you owe, anyone can repay part of your loan and take your collateral in exchange. That is liquidation — automatic, permissionless, and it does not wait for you to answer a phone call. What it feels like. Gold falls over a weekend while you are not watching. Your gold is sold at roughly the worst price of the cycle, you keep the cash you borrowed, and the gold plus every dollar of recovery it would have earned you is gone. A liquidator is paid an incentive to do it, so you end up with less than a voluntary sale at the same price would have left you. What limits it. How far below the maximum you borrow, and how closely you watch. The market Auri uses on Arbitrum has a liquidation loan-to-value of 77%, published on-chain and inspectable by anyone at the XAUt0/USDC market page . Treat 77% as a line to stay well clear of, not a target. Your own liquidation price and health factor are shown live on the loan screen; those are the numbers to act on. Safe 20% Conservative 35% Balanced 55% Risky 77% gold sold at 77% Your share rises when you borrow more, or when gold falls. The gap between your loan-to-value and 77% is your entire buffer — and it collapses as you borrow more. Two loans, same gold, very different outcomes Illustrative, at a round US$4,000/oz with 2 oz of collateral worth US$8,000: Borrow US$3,000 — loan-to-value 37.5%. Gold must fall to about US$1,948/oz, roughly 51%, before liquidation. Borrow US$6,000 — loan-to-value 75%. Gold must fall to about US$3,896/oz, roughly 2.6%. Gold routinely moves that much in a day. Same collateral, same marke

title: Risks
heading: Boost makes all of that much sharper
text: What it is. Boost borrows against gold you hold, immediately buys more gold with the borrowed stablecoins, pledges that too, and repeats to your chosen multiplier. The multiplier sets your loan-to-value directly: 2× is 50%, 3× about 67%, 4× 75%, 5× 80%. What it feels like. Commit US$2,000 of gold at 3× and you hold US$6,000 of exposure with US$4,000 borrowed. Gold up 10% gains about US$600 — 30% on what you committed. Gold down 10% loses about US$600, and a fall of roughly 13% liquidates the position, so the committed gold is gone entirely rather than merely reduced. In a flat market you still pay interest, so doing nothing costs money. What limits it. Only your multiplier, honestly. At 4× the modelled 75% loan-to-value sits about 2.6% below the 77% liquidation level; at 5× it is 80%, above it. The app refuses positions at 82% and higher, but that guard sits above the level at which the underlying market liquidates, so the guard is not what protects you. The liquidation price on the review screen is. If it is within a few percent of today's gold price, do not confirm. Boost sits behind a Pro mode toggle, and you cannot hold a Boost position and a standard loan at once. If you cannot state your liquidation price as a dollar gold price, and cannot afford to lose everything you commit, do not turn Pro mode on. See Boost .

title: Risks
heading: Interest-rate and liquidity risk
text: What it is. The borrow rate is not fixed — the lending market sets it, and it moves with how much of the supplied stablecoin is being borrowed. Available liquidity is finite too, because third parties supply it and can withdraw. What it feels like. Your interest line grows without you having done anything, or Max is a fraction of what you expected because little stablecoin is free that day. What limits it. Visibility, and the right to repay any time with no penalty. Two readings of this market an hour apart in July 2026 gave 3.48% and 3.70%; at that same moment, other gold-collateral markets on the same protocol ranged from 0.27% to 9.47%. A rate you can afford today can double.

title: Risks
heading: Smart-contract and oracle risk
text: What it is. Your loan lives in software, and two things can fail: the lending contracts, and the oracle that tells them what gold is worth. An oracle reporting too low a price triggers liquidations that were not economically justified; too high, and loans grow past the point of being safely collateralised. What it feels like. In the bad version the loss is sudden, total for the affected position, and has no appeals process — no chargeback, no ombudsman, no insurer behind the contract. What limits it. Auri does not run its own lending protocol. It uses Morpho on Arbitrum One, whose per-market contracts are public and immutable and hold third-party funds far beyond Auri's, with market parameters and the oracle address public too. That lowers the risk materially; it does not remove it, and no amount of prior review proves the absence of a bug.

title: Risks
heading: Cross-chain and token-representation risk
text: What it is. Auri's gold is Tether Gold. Native XAUt exists only on Ethereum mainnet; on Arbitrum the asset is XAUt0, the LayerZero OFT version at 0x40461291347e1eCbb09499F3371D3f17f10d7159 . Native XAUt is locked in an adapter on Ethereum and an equal amount of XAUt0 is minted on Arbitrum, so the backing chain is: your XAUt0 → locked XAUt → one troy ounce of vaulted physical gold per token. Every link is a dependency. What it feels like. If the adapter or the cross-chain messaging layer were compromised, XAUt0 could stop being reliably redeemable for the underlying and its price could detach from gold while metal still sits in a vault. You would watch gold rise and the thing you hold not follow. What limits it. It is burn-and-mint against a locked reserve rather than a custodial wrapper, and both contracts are public. But the Arbitrum representation is small — on-chain supply was about 160.7 XAUt0 when we checked in July 2026 — and a thin market means large orders can move the price more than a small quoted impact suggests. Read the price impact on your review screen. More on backing in Reserves and proof .

title: Risks
heading: Stablecoin risk on your cash balance
text: What it is. Your cash balance is not currency in a bank account. It is USDC, issued by Circle on Arbitrum and displayed in your chosen currency; loans are denominated in it too. A stablecoin holds value because its issuer holds reserves and honours redemptions — an undertaking, not a law of nature. What it feels like. A depeg is quiet and fast: your balance reads the same number while that number buys less, and the loan you owe does not shrink to match. Mid-borrow, you are squeezed from both sides at once. What limits it. Circle publishes reserve disclosures and independent attestations on its own site — read them there rather than taking our word for it. Practically: if you are saving, hold gold; if you need dollars soon, withdraw them. A cash balance is a transit account.

title: Risks
heading: None of this is a bank deposit
text: Auri is a non-custodial software platform. It is not a bank, credit union, trust company or deposit-taking institution, and your balances are not deposits. Tokenised gold and stablecoins are not covered by any government or private deposit-insurance, investor-compensation or guarantee scheme, in any jurisdiction . By way of example only: not by the Canada Deposit Insurance Corporation (CDIC) or the Canadian Investor Protection Fund (CIPF) in Canada, and not by the Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation (FDIC), the National Credit Union Administration (NCUA) or the Securities Investor Protection Corporation (SIPC) in the United States. Naming those schemes illustrates protections that do not apply; it does not imply an equivalent applies elsewhere. You can lose money, up to the entire value of your holdings. What you get instead is custody and verifiability: assets in a wallet you control, a named custodian for the metal, public reserve attestations, and a loan book anyone can read. That is a different kind of protection — and note that a reserves attestation is a point-in-time report on specified procedures, not a full audit of the company, and it is silent on any other liabilities the business may have.

title: Risks
heading: Custody and key-loss risk
text: What it is. Self-custody cuts both ways. There is no password to reset because there is no password: access runs through your email or phone, a passkey, an authenticator app and, on mobile, biometrics. On-chain sends cannot be reversed by anyone, Auri included. What it feels like. Two versions, both bad. You change phone and email in the same month, never enrolled a second passkey, never saved your recovery codes — and you are looking at gold you own and cannot reach. Or you paste a wrong address into a withdrawal, confirm, and the funds are simply gone. What limits it. Mostly things you do yourself, before you hold a meaningful amount: enrol two-factor authentication and write the recovery codes somewhere that is not your phone, register more than one passkey on more than one device, keep the biometric lock on, and test any new address with a small amount. Auri also requires step-up authentication before outbound transactions — always for gift, send and remit, and for sales or withdrawals to an external wallet — and restricts bank and instant-rail withdrawals to an account in your own name.

title: Risks
heading: Regulatory and regional availability risk
text: What it is. Auri operates only where it is lawful to do so, and the rules differ by country and, in the United States, by state. Identity verification, fiat rails, currency conversion and card issuance are performed by licensed third parties whose coverage is regional. Regulators can also change their position on tokenised commodities, and on leveraged products in particular. What it feels like. A feature you read about is missing in your region, a rail you relied on stops being offered, or a product you already use becomes unavailable and you unwind a position on someone else's schedule rather than your own. What limits it. Knowing which parts are region-specific before you build a habit on them. Funding rails are not global: Interac e-Transfer is Canada-only, bank transfer is the US equivalent, and the identity check is triggered by the fiat rail you choose — crypto deposits do not require one. Coverage is listed in Reference . Not live yet. The Auri card is a waitlist, not a product — you can join it and see your position, and that is all. Cross-border remittance, the MCP server, the CLI and the public API are also not live. Do not plan around any of them.

title: Risks
heading: Third-party dependency risk
text: What it is. Auri is an interface over other people's infrastructure: Tether issues XAUt and publishes its reserve data. If issuance or redemption stopped, the token's link to metal would be at issue. The vault operator and custodian hold the bars; Auri's app names Brink's in Switzerland. A custody failure puts the backing behind every token in question. The attestation firm checks reserves; Auri's app names BDO Italia. Without a current report, “fully backed” is an assertion rather than a finding. LayerZero / USDT0 run the adapter that makes XAUt0 exist on Arbitrum. Morpho is the lending market, and its capacity currently comes from a very small number of supplying vaults — when we checked, one. If it withdrew, borrowing capacity would shrink sharply. Circle issues the USDC your cash balance and your loan are denominated in. Arbitrum One settles everything; a prolonged outage stalls borrowing, repaying and withdrawing exactly when you most want to act. Exchange liquidity converts stablecoins to gold and back on every buy and sell; thin liquidity shows up as price impact. Licensed fiat and identity partners move money in and out and verify you. Their outages are your outages. What it feels like. Almost always the same symptom whatever the cause: a flow that worked last week returns an error, and the fix is not in Auri's hands. What limits it. These counterparties are named, public and independently verifiable, and every transaction's on-chain legs are traceable from your activity receipt. That lets you diagnose a problem. It does not make you whole if a counterparty fails.

heading: What we can't tell you yet
text: Publishing an unfinished answer beats implying there is no question. These will be filled in here as each is confirmed: Whether customer gold is insured, by which underwriter, against which perils, to what limit — UNKNOWN. title: Risks
heading: When not to use this
text: Do not buy gold with money you need within twelve months, with money that would otherwise clear high-interest debt, or because the price just went up. Do not borrow if the loan funds something you cannot repay out of income, if you will not check the position at least weekly, or if a forced sale at a bad price would genuinely hurt you. Borrowing bridges a timing gap; it does not fund consumption. Do not use Boost if you cannot state your liquidation price as a dollar gold price, if you would not accept losing everything you commit, if you are also running a recurring buy plan (steady accumulation and leverage work against each other), or if you are trying to recover a previous loss. Do not gift or send to someone who cannot complete recipient onboarding — unclaimed gold sits in escrow until claimed or cancelled. See Gift and send .

title: Risks
heading: How you get out
text: To reduce a loan you repay from cash, sell part of the free collateral, or add collateral — three routes, available any time, no early-repayment penalty. To close a Boost position you unwind 25%, 50%, 75% or all of it, which repays the loan and frees the matching gold. To leave entirely: repay, unlock your gold, then either sell to cash and withdraw or move the tokens to a wallet you control. Selling costs 0.49% and a bank payout typically takes one to two business days, so plan a full exit before you need it, not during a drawdown.

title: Reference — fees, limits and parameters
heading: How these figures can change
text: Three different kinds of number appear on this page, and they change in three different ways. Auri's own fees and minimums — the 0.49% buy and sell fee, the 1% debit-card fee, the $10 Auto-Invest minimum, the Jewels and referral rates. Auri sets these and can change them. Percentages hold across currencies; flat amounts and reward values are set per currency and per region. Lending parameters — the borrow rate and the 77% liquidation level. Auri does not set either. The rate is produced continuously by the lending market's interest-rate model in response to how much of the supplied USDC is borrowed, which is why it moves during a single day and why no page should ever describe it as fixed. The liquidation level is fixed in the market's contract; a different level would mean a different market. Both are readable on chain by anyone, at the link above. Availability — which rails and features exist for you depends on where you live. Interac e-Transfer is Canada-only; in the US the equivalent is a bank transfer. Debit-card funding, the card, remittance corridors and tax exports are all regional. Nothing on this page guarantees a feature is available to your account — the app shows you what your account can actually do. When this page and the app disagree, the app is right. It reads live prices, your live health factor and your live liquidation price. This page is a reference for parameters, not a quote. New here? Start at Getting started .
